name: slice-b-buildings
note: Slice B, the BUILDINGS lane (docs/art-pipeline-plan.md §4b; write-up in docs/art/slice-b/buildings.md). Everything is matched to the approved farmhouse, which is the FIRST style ref in styles/elsinore/style.json, so the prompts point at it as 'the first attached image' instead of attaching it twice. Each subject sends the game's OLD drawing (guides/control-*.png, rendered by guides.js) as the 'redraw this, keep its identity' reference, second to last, and its footprint guide LAST: building2.png (2 x 2 crafting stations, the open-air cut-away template), building3.png (3 x 3 closed shops with a hanging picture sign), tree.png (1 x 1 trees with one full tile of headroom). Two candidates of a subject are two subject keys (dairy-a / dairy-b) rather than --n 2, so both land on the contact sheet. Hard budget for the lane: 14 images in round 1 (10 spent); round 2 (2026-10-20) adds 24 more on the same command, keys listed in docs/art/slice-b/buildings.md 'Round 2'. Round-2 refs: the APPROVED oak (_candidates/.../approved/openai--flatter-oak-tree-1.png) for the colour variations, the APPROVED Dairy for the Mill retries, the previous pine draft for the shorter pine, and new controls (general-store, school, bank, dead-tree).

dairy-a.prompt: SUBJECT: the DAIRY, a crafting station where milk is churned into butter and pressed into cheese. CRAFTING-STATION TEMPLATE, shared by every 2 x 2 crafting station in this game: an open-air, cut-away workshop, NOT a closed house. A back wall of the farmhouse's stone-and-plaster runs along the back (top) edge of the footprint; two short side walls of the same stone come forward from its ends about a third of the way; there is NO front wall and NO roof over the front, so the camera looks straight into the workshop. A narrow strip of the farmhouse's golden thatch with its wooden ridge beam sits along the top of the back wall only, like an awning. The floor inside is packed ochre earth with a few flagstones. On that open floor stands the WORK, drawn big and obvious so a player recognises the station at a glance: for the Dairy, a wooden butter churn with its plunger handle, a big round yellow cheese wheel with a wedge cut out on a low wooden table, and a tin milk pail; four white milk bottles in a wooden crate stand against one side wall. Materials, outline, shading, the lower-right contact shadow and the colours are copied from the farmhouse in the FIRST attached image: this station stands in the same village. The second-to-last attached image is the game's OLD drawing of the Dairy: keep what makes it recognisable (the milk bottles in their crate, a touch of its pale blue on the churn's bands and the table) but do NOT copy its closed-house shape; the template above wins. The LAST attached image is a layout guide, a patch of the board grid with a tan 2 x 2 square: the station fills that 2 x 2 square ENTIRELY and stays inside it, back wall along the square's top edge, ground contact on the square's bottom edge, a soft contact shadow to the lower right. Fill the surrounding squares with plain short grass in the style, no props outside the square, and draw the faint grid lines as thin tile edges. Do not leave the tan square tan.
